steps.title: Use the angle in a semicircle

lines.text: $[AB]$ is a diameter, so the angle at $D$ in the semicircle is a right angle.
Triangle $ABD$ is isosceles with the right angle at $D$, so $|AD| = |DB|$ and the two base angles are equal.

skill.output: correct use of theorem, proof, axiom, corollary, converse, implies

steps.title: Statement A: similar triangles must be congruent

lines.text: Tick false.
Similar triangles have the same shape (equal angles) but can be different sizes.
A small triangle and a large triangle can have the same angles, so they are not identical.

steps.title: Statement B: congruent triangles must be similar

lines.text: Tick true.
Congruent triangles have all sides and angles equal, so every feature is identical.
Their angles are therefore the same, which makes them similar.
A parallelogram is a four-sided shape whose opposite sides are parallel and equal in length.
A square has opposite sides parallel and equal in length.
So every square is a parallelogram: the statement is True.

lines.text: Assume that $O$ is inside the triangle $PQR$.
Join $P$ to $O$ and $Q$ to $O$.

steps.title: Bound the angle at the centre

lines.text: If $O$ is inside the triangle, $\angle POQ$ is an angle inside triangle $POQ$, so it is less than a straight angle.

steps.title: Compare with the angle at the circumference

lines.text: The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc $PQ$, so $|\angle PRQ|$ is half of $|\angle POQ|$.
But the angle at $R$ is greater than $90^\circ$. This contradicts the result above, so the assumption is false.
Therefore $O$ cannot be inside the triangle $PQR$.

references.final: O \text{ cannot be inside triangle } PQR

steps.title: Decide whether the statement is true or false

lines.text: "If and only if" means the statement must work in both directions.
Vertically opposite angles are always equal, but equal angles need not be vertically opposite.
So the statement is false.
In an equilateral triangle all three angles are $60^\circ$, so they are equal in size.
These angles are next to each other, not vertically opposite.
So equal angles are not always vertically opposite.
